entries.source_note: KKR's FY2025 Form 10-K drops the conditional its FY2024 filing carried and states affirmatively "We use artificial intelligence and other quantitative analysis tools and models, developed by us and third-party service providers"; no internal use case, team or tool is named anywhere in the filing
entries.title: Annual filing affirms AI use
bullets: KKR replaces earlier conditional wording with an affirmative statement, but names no internal tool or application.

entries.source_note: Announcing a $90M Series C led by KKR, Coder states that at KKR its platform "was rolled out to more than 500 engineers" and that "since first deploying Coder a year ago, the firm has moved from no AI-assisted code to more than half of commits taking place within Coder-managed environments", with CIO Ruchir Swarup quoted that KKR is "now extending these capabilities beyond engineering to analysts, data scientists, and other users" (vendor claim, published by a company KKR was simultaneously investing in)
entries.title: Coder platform reportedly reaches over 500 engineers
bullets: The vendor says over half of commits occur in its environments; KKR was simultaneously investing in the company.

entries.source_note: Counterpoint Global (MSIM) publishes “AI Beneficiaries: Investing in Second-Order Effects”, documenting Culture Quant as its proprietary process built with Harvard Business School academics that “leverages alternative datasets and Morgan Stanley’s Machine Learning Lab”, and stating “we incorporate quantitative tools, such as Culture Quant, when they can complement our investment process” alongside a “Culture Quant AI Beneficiaries Dashboard” (company claim — the paper does not name which machine-learning methods the tool itself runs)
entries.title: Culture Quant supports Counterpoint Global’s investment process
bullets: MSIM describes alternative data and collaboration with its Machine Learning Lab, without specifying the tool’s ML methods.

entries.source_note: Counterpoint Global's “AI’s Hidden Winners” restates that Culture Quant is its proprietary framework, “developed by Counterpoint Global in collaboration with academic experts at Harvard Business School in 2019”, that “leverages alternative datasets and Morgan Stanley’s Machine Learning Lab” and analysed workforce data for more than 300 million employees — the paper's investment conclusions are §1(b) commentary and are not counted toward the stage
entries.title: Culture Quant research describes large workforce dataset
bullets: The paper reiterates the proprietary framework; its investment conclusions are market commentary rather than additional adoption evidence.

entries.source_note: Counterpoint Global begins a live forward-test running “a parallel AI-managed version of its Tailwinds portfolio alongside the human-managed one”, driven by its Golden Swans multi-agent research engine under an OpenAI partnership permitting up to 200 concurrent agents; Morningstar records the team as “transparent that it is too early to draw conclusions on alpha generation”
entries.title: Parallel AI-managed portfolio enters live forward-test
bullets: Golden Swans powers a Tailwinds comparison portfolio; the team says it is too early to assess alpha generation.

entries.source_note: Morningstar Manager Research publishes “AI in Active Fund Management: The State of Adoption in 2026”, whose Counterpoint Global case study — informed by a discovery call with the team — names three proprietary tools built with Morgan Stanley's Machine Learning Research team: Culture Quant, SCIG (PCA/K-means clustering replacing GICS for exposure checks) and Golden Swans (up to 56 parallel persona agents, ~1 hour to a draft initiation report)
entries.title: Morningstar identifies three proprietary research tools
bullets: The case study names Culture Quant, SCIG clustering and Golden Swans agents, including roughly one-hour draft research reports.

entries.source_note: TMAM's own Sustainability Report 2025 states 「当社ではTMAM AIを導入し、既に運用の深化・効率化に繋げており、今後は次世代型AIベースドサービスの模索だけでなく、資産運用事業のサステナビリティを強固にすべく、研究開発も進めています」 — TMAM AI introduced and already contributing to the deepening and efficiency of investment management, with next-generation AI-based services still at exploration/R&D stage (company claim; no user count, adoption rate or output metric disclosed)
entries.title: TMAM AI introduced into investment management
bullets: Tokio Marine claims improved efficiency; next-generation services remain under research and development, with no usage metrics disclosed.

entries.source_note: In a five-party release with Nissay AM, Norinchukin Zenkyoren AM, SOMPO AM and Nowcast announcing the completed generative-AI training curriculum 「AIユースケーススタディ for アセマネ」, TMAM managing executive officer 新村治人 states 「当社は生成AIアプリケーション「TMAM AI」を全社に導入し、運用・営業・コーポレートなどすべての部門における業務の高度化・効率化を推進しています」 and, in the same comment, that raising whole-organisation literacy so that 「一部の社員にとどまらず、全社員が生成AIを日常業務で活用できる」 remains an important challenge; deployment of the curriculum itself is stated in the future tense (company claim)
entries.title: TMAM AI available across all departments
bullets: The firm describes enterprise rollout but says daily use by all employees remains a literacy challenge; the new curriculum is still to be introduced.

entries.source_note: TMAM's own release on strengthening investment capability states 「加えて、運用業務への生成AIの活用も進め運用業務の効率化・高度化を図ってまいります」 — generative AI in investment operations described in the future tense — alongside a plan to grow the investment team from 130 to about 160 people over roughly two years
entries.title: Investment plan anticipates further GenAI use
bullets: Tokio Marine frames expanded applications as future work alongside growth in its investment team.

entries.source_note: USS's Report and Accounts for the year to 31 March 2024 lists trustee-director training during the year on "The impact of Artificial Intelligence on the financial services industry" — board education, no internal use case disclosed anywhere in the document
entries.title: Trustee education covers AI’s financial-services impact
bullets: USS’s annual report records board training without disclosing an internal use case.

entries.source_note: USS's Report and Accounts for the year to 31 March 2025 lists trustee-director training on "Artificial Intelligence (AI) and an update on the scheme's response/plans", the first reference to a scheme-level AI response; the report still discloses no deployed internal AI use case
entries.title: Trustees receive update on scheme AI plans
bullets: The report adds a scheme-level response but still names no deployed internal application.

entries.source_note: USS's Report and Accounts for the year to 31 March 2026 carries a dedicated "Artificial Intelligence (AI) - risks and opportunities" section stating that its software developers use generative coding tools and staff more broadly have access to personal productivity assistants over their documents and emails (company claim — no tool named, no usage figure), alongside a mandatory 'human in the loop' rule, written staff guidelines on safe AI use, enterprise licensing, denial of AI tools to staff handling the most sensitive personal data, an IT/Information Security review gate covering AI tools and business-process agents, and a secure test environment for internal AI 'champions'
entries.title: Coding tools and productivity assistants disclosed
bullets: USS describes access controls, mandatory human review, security approval and a testing environment, without tool names or usage figures.

entries.institution: Amova Asset Management (formerly Nikko Asset Management)
entries.source_note: Amova (then Nikko Asset Management) reports that a quant analyst in its Investment Technology Investment Department won the 「最も革新的なAI活用賞」 at Asia Asset Management's 2024 Best of the Best Awards, and states the firm is focusing on deep-learning research using Japanese-language financial text for sharper analysis of investee companies and markets, better investment performance and more refined ESG evaluation and risk management (company claim)
entries.title: Deep-learning financial-text research receives recognition
bullets: Amova reports an analyst award and research aimed at investment, ESG and risk analysis; benefits are company claims.

entries.institution: Amova Asset Management (formerly Nikko Asset Management)
entries.source_note: In an interview with Wealth Advisor, President and CEO Stefanie Drews says internal communication is conducted bilingually and that AI-based simultaneous interpretation lets ideas be shared from anywhere in the world, and that AI technology is used so an email written in English reaches a Japanese-preferring colleague in Japanese, with all internal documents maintained in both languages (company claim)
entries.title: AI translation supports bilingual internal communication
bullets: The CEO describes simultaneous interpretation and email translation between English and Japanese across the firm.

entries.institution: Amova Asset Management (formerly Nikko Asset Management)
entries.source_note: Amova publishes its Sustainability Report 2025, in which CIO Mark Stoeckle says the firm is strengthening sustainable-investment capability partly through 「ESG分析を強化し、より深い洞察を取り入れた投資判断を行うための高度なAIツールの開発」 — developing advanced AI tools to strengthen ESG analysis and inform investment decisions
entries.title: AI tools under development for ESG analysis
bullets: Amova’s CIO describes research to improve sustainable-investment insights, rather than a completed rollout.

entries.institution: Amova Asset Management (formerly Nikko Asset Management)
entries.source_note: At Amova's 5th Sustainability Townhall, attended by over 430 employees and parent-company staff, CIO Mark Stoeckle outlines recent initiatives including 「投資判断を支援する社内AIソリューションの活用」 — the application of in-house AI solutions to support investment decisions (company claim; no tool, team or user count disclosed)
entries.title: Townhall describes AI support for investment decisions
bullets: The CIO cites internal solutions, but names no tool, team or user count.

entries.institution: Amova Asset Management (formerly Nikko Asset Management)
entries.source_note: Amova publishes its Sustainability Report 2026, which names a firmwide “Accelerated AI Initiative” expanding AI-tool access across the firm and the appointment of AI ambassadors, lists AI as a business-ethics-and-governance materiality sub-theme covering controls around AI deployment, logs “Started development of in-house AI-enabled ESG tools” against 2025, describes the AI-enabled ESG analysis tool begun with the Global Sustainable Investment Team at the end of 2025, and states that a proprietary AI-powered net-zero assessment tool and an emissions attribution framework “are being tested and scheduled for launch in 2026”
entries.title: Accelerated AI Initiative broadens access and training
bullets: Amova names ambassadors and governance work; ESG and net-zero tools remain in development or testing for a planned launch.

entries.source_note: Nest's Members' Panel annual report for 2024–2025 names AI as a new standing topic, stating that "Artificial Intelligence (A.I.) is starting to feature in panel discussion from a wide range of perspectives", asking "Where can A.I. be used positively by Nest to improve member understanding and enhance service delivery?", and committing that "We will continue to incorporate A.I. as an area of future discussion and focus" — an advisory-panel agenda in future tense, with no tool, pilot or deployment named
entries.title: Members’ Panel adds AI to its agenda
bullets: Nest explores potential service and communication benefits without naming a tool, pilot or deployment.

entries.source_note: Nest Corporation's annual report and accounts 2025/26 (period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, ordered to be printed 9 July 2026) discloses that during the 2025/26 financial year "Board members received briefings or training on a number of topics including the Pensions Schemes Bill, customer segmentation and customer strategy, subsidiary governance and oversight, artificial intelligence and investment beliefs" — the first appearance of AI as a Nest board education topic; the same report's only other AI references are to AI as an investment sector and to "AI-driven cyber risk"
entries.title: Board receives AI briefings and training
bullets: The annual report establishes education activity; its other AI mentions concern investment sectors and cyber risk.

entries.source_note: Northern Trust Asset Management announces it has hired 13 quantitative researchers, portfolio analysts and quantitative developers in Amsterdam (largely from APG Asset Management), stating they bring “a successful track record implementing advanced quantitative investing techniques, including deploying machine learning and artificial intelligence, working with alternative data sets”; NTAM reports US$43 billion in quantitative strategies as of 31 December 2024
entries.title: Thirteen quantitative specialists join NTAM
bullets: The hires bring AI, machine-learning and alternative-data experience; the announcement concerns capability building.

entries.source_note: In its 2025 Annual Report Message to Shareholders, Northern Trust reports that the Asset Management business spent the year exploring AI with its investment and distribution teams and names two projects ahead of “a broader rollout in the first quarter of 2026” — a Municipal Bond Transcription AI “designed to monitor issuer calls and distill key insights” that is “currently being refined through active testing”, and a Client Action Plan that “will soon empower those employees serving U.S. institutional clients”; at Corporation level the same letter says accelerated AI deployment “including use of our proprietary NT Byron platform” now handles document ingestion and reconciliation (company claims; the document carries no printed publication date)
entries.title: Bond transcription and client-plan tools enter testing
bullets: NTAM plans broader rollout in 2026; separate NT Byron deployment claims relate to the parent corporation.

entries.source_note: Northern Trust Corporation's 2026 proxy statement discloses board-level AI governance: “the Board provides oversight of the Corporation's use of artificial intelligence (‘AI’) as part of its broader oversight of strategy, technology, and risk management” through “regular management updates on AI initiatives”, records that management “Advanced the firm's enterprise artificial intelligence program, reinforcing governance and use-case discipline”, and notes a newly stood-up Technology and Operations Committee
entries.title: Parent board formalizes AI oversight
bullets: Northern Trust Corporation discloses management updates, governance discipline and a new Technology and Operations Committee.

entries.source_note: Investor Daily reports NTAM president Michael Hunstad at SuperReview's CIO roundtable in Melbourne on 11 March 2026 describing AI inside the investment process: NLP applied to patent and trademark databases “in any language” to profile a company's intellectual property and its momentum, AI-powered “network mapping” of clients, vendors and peer ecosystems, and AI-driven strategies with information ratios above one over more than five years (company claim, no AUM given); Hunstad states “the first rule of quantitative investing, which is now inclusive of AI, is never, ever let your model make the decision” and says an agentic portfolio manager for process-oriented functions such as passive indexation is something “we're working on”
entries.title: NTAM describes NLP and network mapping in investing
bullets: The president cites patent analysis and AI strategies but retains human decisions; an agentic portfolio manager is still being developed.

entries.source_note: On the Q1 2026 earnings call, CEO Michael O'Grady says “AI is increasingly embedded in how we operate” and sets out an AI strategy “anchored in three outcomes: hyper-personalization, AI-generated alpha, and infinite scalability”, stating that “Within asset management, AI-assisted research and product construction tools are enabling teams to process significantly larger structured and unstructured data sets, identify patterns more quickly, and test scenarios more efficiently” (company claim; no penetration or use-case count disclosed)
entries.title: AI-assisted research and product tools described
bullets: Northern Trust’s CEO claims faster analysis and scenario testing within asset management, without adoption or use-case counts.

entries.source_note: Northern Trust Asset Management launches two actively managed UCITS funds applying the NT Adaptive Equity strategy, stating that “Advanced analytical techniques, including natural language processing, are used to identify idiosyncratic opportunities that the market may overlook”, with early investment from a Nordic institutional investor; NTAM reports US$47 billion in quantitative strategies and US$1.4 trillion total AUM as of 31 March 2026
entries.title: Adaptive Equity UCITS funds launch
bullets: NTAM says NLP helps identify overlooked opportunities, with initial investment from a Nordic institution.

entries.source_note: On the Q2 2026 earnings call, O'Grady says “the conversation around AI has moved from experimentation to execution”, that “In our asset management business, for example, we're using AI to enhance our investment research and idea generation, uncovering signals that may be overlooked by traditional industry approaches” and that “These capabilities are embedded most directly in our adaptive equity quant strategies”; he cites “client action plan agents that help relationship managers quickly synthesize data” and cyber “horizon scanning agents” as proof points, describes AI as “augmented intelligence” and states the work “is built on a foundation of human oversight and accountability” (company claims; no penetration or daily-use figure given)
entries.title: Earnings call links AI research to adaptive equities
bullets: Management also names client-action and cyber agents, emphasizing human oversight; usage and penetration figures are absent.

entries.source_note: Nuveen announces it is acquiring direct-indexing manager Brooklyn Investment Group and its parent technology company Brooklyn Artificial Intelligence, Inc.; Nuveen's release describes Brooklyn as combining "artificial intelligence with institutional-grade portfolio optimization and automated tax-loss harvesting", and names white-label licensing of that technology to other firms as one of three priority initiatives (company claim)
entries.title: Brooklyn acquisition adds AI-enabled direct indexing
bullets: Nuveen describes portfolio optimization and tax-loss harvesting capabilities, alongside plans to license the technology externally.

entries.source_note: Nuveen Asset Management's Form ADV Part 2A brochure states that "NAM utilizes artificial intelligence technologies, including machine learning and generative artificial intelligence" as part of "our investment and business processes" — research, tax optimization and/or trading support for certain strategies, and support, administrative and ancillary functions — under "written policies and governance structures", with portfolio managers retaining final decision-making authority; the same brochure says Tax Advantaged Strategies "leverage artificial intelligence and technology-driven optimization to identify rebalancing and tax loss harvesting opportunities". The March 2025 brochure contained no mention of artificial intelligence
entries.title: Regulatory brochure affirms investment and business AI use
bullets: Nuveen names research, tax and trading support under written governance, with portfolio managers retaining final decisions.

entries.source_note: Nuveen fund registration statement (Nushares ETF Trust, Form 485BPOS) adds a "Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools" risk factor disclosing that Nuveen Fund Advisors and Nuveen Asset Management "may rely on programs and systems that utilize AI, machine learning, probabilistic modeling and other data science technologies" in their business operations — permissive rather than affirmative wording
entries.title: Fund filing adds permissive AI risk language
bullets: The registration statement says advisers may use AI systems; it does not establish a new deployment.

entries.source_note: Ontario Teachers' 2023 annual report describes a cross-fund approach to identifying AI use cases and running experiments, with CIO Stephen McLennan naming AI as a way of "increasing the productivity of our teams" — experiments, no shipped internal system disclosed
entries.title: Cross-fund AI experiments focus on team productivity
bullets: Ontario Teachers’ annual report describes use-case discovery and testing without a shipped internal system.

entries.source_note: Ontario Teachers' 2024 annual report states the fund rolled out AI tools to all employees to drive workforce efficiencies and introduced dedicated AI champions across the fund (company claim — no tool named, no adoption or usage figure disclosed)
entries.title: AI tools reportedly rolled out to all employees
bullets: Ontario Teachers names an AI champions network, but provides no tool names or usage figures.

entries.source_note: Ontario Teachers' 2025 annual report discloses the launch of Clarity, a generative-AI internal virtual assistant for Member Services that provides a secure access point to knowledge sources and process support and helps team members onboard and resolve member inquiries more quickly (company claim); the same report says the fund "continued to experiment with AI across the organization"
entries.title: Clarity launches for Member Services
bullets: The internal GenAI assistant supports knowledge access, onboarding and inquiries; wider organizational experimentation continues.

entries.source_note: Benefits and Pensions Monitor, reporting Chief Investment Officer Gillian Brown's interview at the Bloomberg Canadian Finance Conference, writes that Ontario Teachers' is actively integrating AI into its processes, particularly for data analysis, market scans and internal communications (company claim, secondary report — the Bloomberg original was not readable)
entries.title: CIO describes AI in data analysis and communications
bullets: Secondary coverage reports active integration and market scanning; the original Bloomberg interview was unavailable for review.

entries.source_note: Ontario Teachers' appoints Feifei Wu to the newly established role of Senior Managing Director, Investment Technology & Applied Intelligence, leading the fund's AI strategy to strengthen governance and accelerate adoption, reporting to CTO Terry Hickey
entries.title: Applied Intelligence leadership role created
bullets: Feifei Wu joins as Senior Managing Director to lead AI strategy, governance and adoption, reporting to the CTO.

entries.source_note: An Ontario Teachers' job posting on its own Workday careers board names an internal "AI Centre of Excellence" as a standing partner function alongside Enterprise Data, Platform Engineering and Enterprise Security, and carries the fund's standing disclosure that it may use AI-based tools to screen and assess job applicants while stating that its use of AI does not replace human decision-making
entries.title: Job advertisement names an AI Centre of Excellence
bullets: The posting also allows possible AI-assisted applicant screening while retaining human decisions; it does not establish screening deployment.

entries.source_note: UTIMCO's Hedge Funds and Fixed Income team presents its 2025 Action Plan to the Board of Directors; under “Systems” it commits to “explore how to incorporate AI into workflow” and to “Explore Copilot capabilities and test other forms of AI into workflow to enhance existing processes” — the only AI item in UTIMCO's own board materials since 2023
entries.title: Board action plan commits to AI exploration
bullets: UTIMCO’s investment team plans to test Copilot and other workflow tools, without claiming a shipped application.

entries.source_note: Pensions & Investments reports UTIMCO's 6 March 2026 board meeting and, in the same article, its staff AI programme: UTIMCO “will be focused on improving AI skills among its staff of about 130 people” through a five-tier framework running from shared language, responsible use cases and “risks and limitations … including hallucinations”, through everyday efficiency gains, to department-specific applications and, last, leadership “oversight and accountability”; chief human resources officer Alison Rogers-McCoy says “No organization has a perfect playbook” and that “there are people in our organization really using” AI “to solve real problems in their workflow” (company claim — no tool, team or deployment named)
entries.title: Staff AI program sets five levels of capability
bullets: UTIMCO targets skills and responsible use for about 130 staff; anecdotal workflow benefits come without named tools or deployment counts.

entries.source_note: UTIMCO posts an Operational Due Diligence Analyst requisition (OPERA001160, updated 27 August 2026) that lists among the role's responsibilities “Identify process improvements and leverage AI tools to enhance efficiency and scalability of ODD workflows”
entries.title: Due-diligence analyst role includes AI workflow improvement
bullets: The vacancy asks for efficiency and scalability through AI; it is a hiring signal, not proof of completed work.

entries.source_note: UTIMCO posts a Data & AI Solutions Engineer requisition (DATAA001161) scoping generative-AI work inside its own stack — “Integrate Azure OpenAI Service capabilities into enterprise applications within UTIMCO's secure Azure environment”, “Design and implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions using approved enterprise data sources”, and development of “evaluation, testing, and monitoring processes that support quality, traceability, and responsible AI deployment”
entries.title: Data and AI engineer vacancy scopes Azure OpenAI work
bullets: Responsibilities include enterprise integration, retrieval-augmented generation, evaluation and monitoring; the role describes planned work.

entries.source_note: UTIMCO posts a Director, Hedge Fund Investments requisition (DIREC001163) requiring “Proficiency in applying artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve research, analysis, communication, and workflow efficiency, with sound judgment regarding accuracy, confidentiality, and appropriate use”, and stating that the role “requires advanced financial-tool and responsible artificial intelligence (AI) proficiency”
entries.title: Hedge-fund director vacancy requires responsible AI proficiency
bullets: The posting names research, analysis and workflow use, with accuracy and confidentiality requirements.

entries.source_note: UTIMCO posts an Associate, Private Equity Funds requisition (ASSOC001162) listing as a preferred qualification “Proficiency leveraging AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot) to enhance productivity, automate workflows, accelerate research, and improve day-to-day productivity” — the only place UTIMCO names the tools
entries.title: Private-equity vacancy names ChatGPT and Copilot
bullets: The associate role prefers experience using these tools for research and productivity; it does not establish current deployment.

entries.source_note: At Texas TRS's July 2025 board meeting, senior managing director for private markets Eric Lang tells trustees in a private markets presentation that his team “was looking at how AI might be helpful in forecasting performance in private equity”, saying AI “has the potential to help us manage those investments” over five-to-ten-year holds and that “we're very focused on trying to get the best tools in our team's hands” — exploration of a use case, with no deployment claimed
entries.title: Private-markets team explores AI performance forecasting
bullets: Texas TRS discusses potential value for long-term private-equity investments, without claiming deployment.

entries.source_note: Texas TRS's $6.2 billion emerging manager programme adopts Microsoft Copilot in its own workflow — “The program has been using Microsoft Copilot… to help in manager evaluation, researching and even engaging with prospective firms largely with the help of the team's early career talent” — after integrating AI “to streamline internal processes” was set among the team's goals for 2025; head of programme Kirk Sims says he expects AI use “to continue to grow as TRS absorbs these capabilities more”
entries.title: Emerging-manager program uses Microsoft Copilot
bullets: Texas TRS describes manager evaluation, research and engagement support, with further adoption expected.

entries.source_note: At the 12 February 2026 board meeting, executive director Brian Guthrie tells trustees they “will be able to produce AI-generated summaries of meeting agenda items while also using an AI tool to answer questions about the material”; administrative staff encourage trustees to use AI “to assist — but not replace — their own review of materials”, and investment staff are reported to have “noted current uses as well as intentions of finding ways to use AI in investment process”
entries.title: Trustees offered AI summaries and document questions
bullets: Staff emphasize assistance rather than replacement of trustees’ own review; investment uses and future intentions are also mentioned.

entries.source_note: Wellcome co-signs the Research Funders Policy Group's first joint statement on the use of generative AI tools in funding applications and assessment, its first published governance position on generative AI in its own funding process (date taken from the current revision of the page, which records “Statement first published September 2023”)
entries.title: Joint policy addresses GenAI in funding assessment
bullets: Wellcome co-signs the research-funders statement, establishing a governance position for its funding process.

entries.source_note: Wellcome's annual report for the year to 30 September 2024 states that “a new policy on the use of artificial intelligence will be launched in 2025” — future tense — and records “AI-powered coaching” as part of the LinkedIn Learning platform provided to staff
entries.title: AI policy planned alongside staff coaching access
bullets: The annual report anticipates a 2025 policy and records AI-powered coaching through LinkedIn Learning.

entries.source_note: Wellcome publishes its annual report for the year to 30 September 2025, recording an internal audit covering “AI governance”, a sustainability review of “the impact and mitigation possibilities related to our use of AI tools”, a programme that “began” moving Wellcome Collection's collections and library management systems to “AI-enabled systems”, and a firm-level risk mitigation of “Exploring how AI can enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of Wellcome's work”
entries.title: Annual report records AI governance audit and systems work
bullets: Wellcome describes review of AI impacts and an early move toward AI-enabled collections systems.

entries.source_note: Wellcome's generative AI funding policy, last updated 8 April 2026, states that “Wellcome staff have access to a limited number of enterprise data protected (EDP) generative AI tools” and that grant-application information “may be entered into them for processing purposes, for example, to assess scheme eligibility or remit”, while stating that Wellcome does “not use generative AI tools to assess the quality of grant applications or to aid funding decisions” (company claim — no tool is named and no usage figure is given)
entries.title: Protected GenAI tools permitted for application processing
bullets: Wellcome allows limited administrative uses but explicitly excludes assessing application quality or aiding funding decisions.

entries.source_note: Research Professional News reports that at the ARMA conference on 18 June 2026 representatives of Wellcome and UKRI said the Research Funders Policy Group would update its joint position so funders “may use generative AI to process funding applications” with all final decisions taken by humans, and quotes Wellcome senior funding policy adviser Sue Russell saying the funder would not pass applicant AI-disclosure data to its grants committees
entries.title: Funders plan revised AI-processing policy
bullets: Conference coverage describes possible application processing with final human decisions, rather than a new deployment at Wellcome.

entries.source_note: Business Insider publishes an on-the-record Q&A with CIO and Head of Technology Transformation Lúcia Soares describing Carlyle's internal AI rollout across 2,300 employees: “90% of our employees use tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Copilot”, AI training from an employee's first day, an AI champions' council, Project Catalyst workflow automation, credit investors assessing a company “in hours” rather than weeks, AI review of legal invoices with “real savings”, investment-committee memos required into an AI tool in some business lines, and a standing rule that “we never allow AI to make a final decision” (penetration and savings are company claims)
entries.title: Carlyle reports AI use by 90% of employees
bullets: The CIO names research, memo and legal workflows, plus training and champions; final decisions remain human and savings are company claims.

entries.source_note: Anthropic's “Agents for financial services” announcement quotes Carlyle Chief Digital Officer Matt Anderson: “Carlyle has adopted Claude as a key part of our AI technology stack because of its strong coding capabilities, agentic reasoning, and continual advances in both the underlying models and key features. Claude is a core tool for delivering value across our firm from investing to operations to portfolio management” (company claim, vendor-published; no penetration or use-case detail given)
entries.title: Claude described as core to Carlyle’s AI stack
bullets: A vendor-published company statement cites investing and operations, but provides no penetration or detailed use-case figures.

entries.source_note: Carlyle joins the MIT Generative AI Impact Consortium as a founding-tier member; MIT's consortium site states Carlyle “will support research across areas like finance, economics, artificial intelligence and quantitative methods” and quotes CEO Harvey Schwartz saying Carlyle sees “significant potential to use it to make better-informed investment decisions” by combining its proprietary private-markets data with “the judgment of our investors and advances in AI” — forward-looking, and counted as strategic-priority context rather than deployment
entries.title: MIT consortium membership supports future AI research
bullets: Carlyle frames better investment decisions as potential, making this strategic-priority context rather than deployment evidence.

entries.source_note: FY2025/26 report, 'Building an AI-Native GIC' (p.25): dates ChatGIC's rollout 'across the enterprise' to 2023; names an AI Research Assistant over GIC's internal knowledge and 'a virtual Investment Committee member that evaluates and challenges investment proposals'; describes a recently launched enterprise AI platform integrating 'Claude and GPT' with GIC's internal data under an AI Council co-chaired by the COO and CRO; states GIC is 'moving from being AI-enabled to becoming AI-native' (company claims)
entries.title: Annual report sets out an AI-native push
bullets: GIC dates ChatGIC's enterprise rollout to 2023 and names an AI Research Assistant, a virtual Investment Committee member and a Claude/GPT enterprise platform governed by an AI Council (company claims).
The report states GIC is moving from AI-enabled to AI-native; no user count or adoption rate is disclosed.

entries.source_note: Launches Nadia, an AI-enabled coach with GIC-specific context available to every employee, which the FY2025/26 report (p.67) says has held 'close to 4,000 conversations' since launch; the same report (p.66) makes AI 'a core module in our new hire programme' (company claims)
entries.title: Nadia AI coach launched for all staff
bullets: An AI-enabled coach with GIC-specific context is available to every employee; the FY2025/26 report counts close to 4,000 conversations since launch (company claim).
AI becomes a core module of the new-hire programme.

entries.source_note: CTO Umesh Subramanian tells Reuters, in an interview at the Reuters Next conference, that the Citadel AI Assistant — a chatbot trained on licensed transcripts, regulatory filings, brokerage research and the firm's own investment strategies — "has been rolled out inside the firm over the past year" and "is now used regularly by nearly all of its equities investors", adding that "investment judgment still remains in human hands" (company claim; Reuters, by Milana Vinn)
entries.title: CTO tells Reuters the AI Assistant reaches nearly all equities investors
bullets: Rolled out inside the firm over the past year and used regularly by nearly all equities investors, per Umesh Subramanian; investment judgment stays in human hands (company claim).
Reuters' own interview is the primary disclosure; the article gives no other business line, user count or daily-use figure.
